description: Prioritized execution queue for repository-wide cognitive reclassification. All items require metadata-only changes (CognitiveLevel + DifficultyScore). Zero content, stem, choice, explanation, or answer-key changes.
governance_rule: Governance-guard Rule 5 — max 30 question objects per change-set

execution_phases.label: Phase 0 — Structural Defect Fixes (IMMEDIATE)
execution_phases.rationale: Items with HO labels that are structurally unrenderable. Must be addressed before any reclassification.

items_list.issue: All fields empty — stem, choices, and correct choice absent. Carries question_state: Certified.
items_list.action: Archive immediately. Remove from Certified pool. Catalog in DEFECT_LIBRARY.md if not already documented.

items_list.issue: Additional structural defects identified in S93P (2 more, ~3 total projected).
items_list.action: Per-item audit to confirm. Fix or archive.
Per-item audit to confirm. Fix or archive.

execution_phases.notes: These items block accurate reporting and should not carry any cognitive label. Per DEFECT_LIBRARY.md DL-034 precedent: structural defects with Certified state should be immediate-fix priority.

execution_phases.label: Phase 1 — Tier 1 (Order-of-Magnitude Errors: Remember/Understand → Evaluate/Analyze)
execution_phases.rationale: Definition-to-term matching or single-concept classification items labeled as Analyze/Evaluate. Most egregious misclassification — 4+ tiers overstated in some cases. Seven of EC's 66 HO items are this category.

sections.evidence: S96P pilot: EC-005 (segregation of duties), EC-020 (physical control classification), EC-008 (COSO framework definition) — all definition-matching.
sections.note: S96P pilot already audited all 75 items.

sections.evidence: 4/4 sampled items are concept comprehension (common-size, EVA, TQM, cost-benefit). Stem defines the concept. Answer is the term.
3/3 sampled items are definition-to-term matching (kaizen costing, reciprocal method, normal costing).
ASC rule application (P1-A-012: ASC 450; P1-A-039: depreciation formula). Deterministic standard application.
Scattered across Pack B and Pack E. Per-item verification required. Extrapolated from S93P per-pack accuracy rates.

execution_phases.label: Phase 2 — Tier 2 (One-Tier Slippage: Apply → Analyze, Analyze → Evaluate)
execution_phases.action: Downgrade by one tier (Evaluate → Analyze, or Analyze → Apply)
execution_phases.rationale: Formula substitution, procedure execution, or COSO classification items labeled one tier too high. Content is well-written — relabel only.

sections.evidence: Formula-execution items reframed as Analyze. Genuine trade-off items correctly labeled. Section-level accuracy: 60-71%.
COSO classification items: 'Which COSO component does X support?' — classified as Analyze, should be Apply. Genuine COSO diagnosis items correctly labeled.

S96P pilot: EC-007 (diagnosing control environment), EC-011 (risk assessment failure). Genuine scenario-based items that ask the candidate to identify what went wrong (Analyze), not to make a recommendation (Evaluate).
Formula substitution (EVA, FOH volume variance, ABC allocation) labeled as Analyze/Evaluate. Per-item verification required.
ASC rule application items overstated by one tier.
Scattered across Sections C, D, E. Mixed patterns. Per-item verification required.
Scattered across Pack B (formula substitution) and Pack E (different pipeline).

execution_phases.label: Phase 3 — Tier 3 (Verification of Accurately Labeled Items)
execution_phases.action: Verify and document — no changes expected
execution_phases.rationale: Items that passed the gate during pilot or project to be correctly labeled. Per-item spot-check verification only.

sections.evidence: 83% Evaluate accuracy. Genuine evaluative trade-off items. S77 campaign benchmark.
sections.action: Spot-check 5 items. Confirm labels. Document as gold standard exemplars.

sections.evidence: 100% Evaluate accuracy. Technology governance — inherently evaluative.
sections.action: Spot-check 2 items. Confirm labels. Gold standard.

sections.evidence: Best modernization campaign. 71% Evaluate, 60% Analyze accuracy. Many genuinely evaluative.
sections.action: Spot-check 10 items. Confirm labels for items not in Phase 2.

sections.evidence: Mixed sections. Items with high probability of correct labeling.
sections.action: Spot-check per section. Verify against gate criteria. Document.

execution_order.note: Must be resolved before Phase 1 — accurate reporting requires zero dead items in HO pool.
Highest-leverage correction. 56 items account for ~18% of the total overstatement but are the most egregious. Definition-matching → Remember/Understand.
Formula substitution, procedure execution, classification items. Per-item audit required for LOW-confidence sections.
Spot-check verification. No changes expected for HIGH-confidence sections. Per-item audit for LOW-confidence sections.

difficulty_calibration_note: Many HO-labeled items also carry inflated difficulty scores. When downgrading CognitiveLevel, also review DifficultyScore for consistency: Evaluate → minimum Moderate (3), Analyze → minimum Moderate (2), Apply at Easy (1) is valid. Items like EC-031 (Risk appetite, labeled Very Difficult(1) = inconsistency — DifficultyScore 1 is impossible for Evaluate).
deliverable_format: Each batch produces: (1) Per-item before/after CognitiveLevel and DifficultyScore, (2) Confidence level (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), (3) Evidence from S95P rubrics, (4) Batch summary with QID list. All changes logged to REVISION_HISTORY.md per governance best practice.

governance_notes.revision_history_note: CognitiveLevel changes are not question_state changes per governance-guard Rule 1, but best practice is to log all label corrections to REVISION_HISTORY.md.
governance_notes.certification_impact: None. Changing CognitiveLevel does not invalidate CAQS §1.7.2 certification. Content (stem, choices, explanations, answer key) is unchanged. Suggested amendment: items with 2+ tier downgrade should flag for lower-confidence re-verification on CAQS Dimension 2 (Cognitive Level).
